target.title: fix(music): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where music generation providers (e.g. fal) could hang forever when a CDN returned response headers and then dripped the audio body slowly enough to keep resetting the per-chunk idle timer. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body — including non-2xx error-detail reads inside shared `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset`, one wall-clock deadline now spans headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` / `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`, matching the Vydra / Discord probe hang-floor shape.

Header fetch still goes through `fetchProviderOperationResponse` (keeps transient download retries). `requestFailedMessage` is omitted on purpose so shared `assertOkOrThrowHttpError` cannot consume a dripping error body without a wall-clock bound before this helper's timed readers run.

Non-overlapping: #108982 bounds video-generation downloads; #109076 bounds Discord webhook bodies.

Collision check: no open hang-class PR on `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset` / `src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts`.

## User Impact

Generated music URL downloads fail within the configured timeout when a remote body keeps trickling instead of completing — for both 2xx asset bodies and dripping non-2xx error bodies. Music generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

## Evidence

Exact head: `ff9b5610ddfbab81b4478f4c32b50d2d6e5572ac`

`oxfmt --check src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```

 ✓ bounds a dripping non-2xx error body with one wall-clock deadline 256ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 407ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Loopback proof

```bash
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx proof-music-download-deadline.mts
```

```
head=ff9b5610ddfbab81b4478f4c32b50d2d6e5572ac
node=v22.22.0
  ok: drip body (200) is bounded by wall-clock deadline
  ok: error mentions timeout
  ok: error mentions timeoutMs
  ok: elapsed within budget
  info: case=200-drip elapsed_ms=261 timeout_ms=250
  ok: drip error body (500) is bounded by wall-clock deadline
  ok: error mentions timeout
  ok: elapsed within budget
  info: case=500-drip elapsed_ms=253 timeout_ms=250
  ok: negative control: idle-only on drip stays unsettled past 400ms
  info: case=negative-control settled=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed
```

- **Drip body (200)**: continuous 20ms chunk drip with `timeoutMs: 250` rejects in 261ms — wall-clock deadline covers body, not just headers.
- **Drip non-2xx body (500)**: continuous 20ms drip with `timeoutMs: 250` rejects in 253ms — error-detail body reads also bounded.
- **Negative control**: idle-only `chunkTimeoutMs: 100` on a 20ms drip stays unsettled past 400ms — proves the old code path has no wall-clock bound.

### Not tested

Live fal CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

- 7/7 tests passed in `live-test-helpers.test.ts` including emoji boundary preservation test

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low
"

target.title: fix(clawhub): keep request deadline through response body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gap where ClawHub request deadlines were cleared at HTTP headers, leaving stalled or dripping response bodies unbounded. Fixes a compatibility issue where the previous revision applied the same 30s wall-clock deadline to large (up to 256 MiB) archive downloads, which could terminate a healthy progressing transfer.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clawhubRequest` previously cleared its `AbortController` timer as soon as `fetch` returned headers, so `readResponseWithLimit` per-chunk idle detection was the only body bound — a slow drip could keep resetting chunk-idle and hang forever.

This change keeps the wall-clock deadline through body consumption for all paths, but archive downloads (`downloadClawHubPackageArchive`, `downloadClawHubSkillArchive`, `downloadClawHubSkillArchiveUrl`, `downloadClawHubGitHubSkillArchive`) release it after headers via a new `releaseAfterHeaders` option. Per-chunk idle detection in `readClawHubResponseBytes` still bounds stalls for all paths.

Non-goals: changing `readClawHubResponseBytes` or `readResponseWithLimit` internals, changing the default 30s budget.

Collision check: no open PR on `src/infra/clawhub.ts` with overlapping deadline semantics.

## User Impact

- Stalled or continuously dripping ClawHub metadata/JSON responses fail with the request wall-clock deadline instead of hanging.
- Archive downloads (skill, package, ClawPack, GitHub source) are not cut off at the 30s metadata budget; a progressing transfer completes while per-chunk idle detection still terminates stalled bodies.
- Retry, error-body, and JSON paths keep the full-body wall-clock.

## Evidence

Exact head: `ecb99af3b605822264d8e0c1d8a76db8f8dcd026`

`oxfmt --check src/infra/clawhub.ts src/infra/clawhub.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/clawhub.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```

 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > aborts ClawHub JSON bodies that drip past the request deadline 52ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled skill archive body reads 11ms

 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > lets a progressing archive body survive past the request deadline 6ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  83 passed | 2 skipped (85)
```

### Contract

| Path | Wall-clock | Chunk-idle | Stall bound |
|------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| Metadata/JSON (`fetchJson`, `parseClawHubJsonBody`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Error bodies (`readErrorBody`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Skill card (`fetchClawHubSkillCard`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Promotions feed (`fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| **Archive downloads** | **released at headers** | 30s | **chunk-idle** |

### New test: progressing archive survives past request deadline

- `downloadClawHubSkillArchive` with `timeoutMs: 50`, `releaseAfterHeaders: true`, body drips every 10ms (10 chunks) via fake timers
- `abortCount: 0` — request deadline was not triggered
- Transfer completes with valid `sha256Hex` — progressing body not falsely terminated

Live ClawHub CDN against real archive endpoints — requires real ClawHub auth token.

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750
Follow-up: #105877

## Current Status

The implementation and validation work is complete on the frozen final range:

```text
base: ee80377a22b36b1bff6faed20c9233134e2a186d
head: edc24088387a8d573798233979a71f3b40a24ac9
```

The branch intentionally stays on that reviewed and verified baseline. It will not continue chasing later `main` movement. GitHub currently reports the PR as `CONFLICTING / DIRTY` because `main` advanced again after the final rebase; that repository-level conflict is the only known landability blocker.

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart could repeatedly select the same interrupted main session for automatic recovery. The existing retry loop was process-local, so supervisor backoff only delayed the next attempt: a session that never became healthy could be dispatched again after every restart without a durable ceiling.

This PR adds a durable, session-owned recovery fuse. The first three accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recovery attempts may dispatch. Before a fourth dispatch, OpenClaw persists an operator notice, tombstones the session, and requires recovery through inspection and `/new` or reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Recovery ownership

The durable state is the core-internal `InternalSessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` aggregate, separate from the public `SessionEntry` contract. It records the recovery cycle and revision, charged attempts, the exact pre-dispatch reservation, lifecycle-generation foreground claim tokens, and an optional terminal tombstone.

`src/agents/main-session-recovery-state.ts` owns the pure transitions. `src/agents/main-session-recovery-store.ts` owns atomic persistence against the canonical SQLite row. Gateway and direct agent-command ingress use the same identity, revision, reservation, lifecycle-generation, and foreground-owner rules.

The policy is:

- persist the charge and reservation before dispatch;
- roll back only when the exact request is known not to have been accepted;
- retain the charge when acceptance is uncertain, including a stale reservation after restart;
- allow three charged attempts, then persist the notice and tombstone before a fourth dispatch;
- do not reset the budget merely because time passes; and
- clear it after healthy non-aborted settlement, session replacement, or reset.

`restartRecoveryRuns` remains a lifecycle-generation fence rather than the durable retry budget. Subagent orphan recovery remains independently owned and retains its existing policy.

### Concurrency and restart safety

The final implementation includes:

- lifecycle-generation fences so stale cleanup cannot erase new work;
- Gateway recovery leases bound to the exact recovery identity;
- snapshot revision and foreground-claim checks around concurrent admission;
- stale lifecycle-clear suppression after tombstoning;
- predecessor preclaims during freshness rollover;
- exact reservation rollback across session-key canonicalization; and
- transcript-only exhaustion notice persistence before tombstoning, with retry when notice persistence fails.

### Plugin SDK boundary

Recovery coordination remains internal and does not become a plugin contract.

- Public session reads project internal rows to `SessionEntry`.
- Modern patch/upsert APIs strip escaped private input and preserve internal recovery state.
- Deprecated `loadSessionStore` and `updateSessionStore` now also project public rows and reconcile public mutations while preserving private recovery state and deletion semantics.
- The public testing result excludes the internal recovery candidate.
- The generated Plugin SDK surface contains no recovery-internal concept, and no checksum-only baseline update hides a semantic change.

The broader shipped Plugin SDK testing-barrel question remains tracked separately in #105877.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three charged accepted or acceptance-uncertain attempts, OpenClaw persists the operator notice and quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch. Healthy progress, replacement, or reset restores the full budget; waiting alone does not.

Plugins continue to see the public session contract and cannot observe or accidentally overwrite the internal recovery state through either modern or deprecated session-store APIs.

## Evidence

Exact frozen range:

```text
ee80377a22b36b1bff6faed20c9233134e2a186d..edc24088387a8d573798233979a71f3b40a24ac9
```

- Focused final regression set: 227 tests passed (`14` recovery-state, `15` Gateway lifecycle, `198` agent tests).
- Broader restart-recovery suite: 86 passed.
- Agent-command suite: 112 passed.
- Core production and test `tsgo` lanes passed.
- Targeted and changed-file `oxfmt` / `oxlint` passed.
- LOC ratchet passed for all 53 changed production TypeScript files.
- Full changed-file gate passed against the frozen base, including core/extension types, lint, Plugin SDK surface/API/exports, and repository guards.
- Full local build passed on Node `24.15.0`.
- Mandatory default-Codex Auto Review covered the final change in six synthetic slices plus the final dirty follow-up; no accepted/actionable finding remains.
- Thread-aware GitHub inspection found no unresolved inline review threads; the current maintainer review decision is `APPROVED`.

Final end-to-end proof used a local Docker container, actual provider `local-container`, lease `cbx_9736f8111fa1`, Ubuntu 26.04:

- complete container build passed;
- a real Gateway started successfully;
- exhausted recovery ended with `status=failed`, `abortedLastRun=false`, and `chargedAttempts=3`;
- the transcript notice was persisted; and
- the tombstone was written before any fourth dispatch.

Exact-head GitHub automation has passed the dependency and security guards plus one real-behavior proof run. The standard full CI workflow did not dispatch for this fork-head update. Exact-merge-result CI cannot exist while GitHub reports the later-main conflict.

## Known Blocker

The code, tests, review findings, and exact-head behavior proof are complete. GitHub currently reports `mergeable=CONFLICTING` and `mergeStateStatus=DIRTY` after `main` advanced again. Per the frozen-branch decision, this PR will not be rebased or merged with another moving `main` baseline.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve thinking default precedence for listed agents
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 17, 2026, 12:05 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:05 UTC.
Last body edit: July 17, 2026, 12:09 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:09 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 16, 2026, 11:58 PM (US Eastern Time) / 03:58 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #109276

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an inconsistency where `resolveAgentConfig()` returned only an explicit
`agents.list[].thinkingDefault` value even though its contract says that agent
defaults have already been applied. Callers that inspect the resolved config
could therefore observe `undefined` for a listed agent while the effective
runtime later inherited `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` through another
resolution path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct nullish fallback suggested by the issue is incomplete on its own.
Several runtime callers intentionally treat the value from the agent entry as
an explicit override before evaluating per-model `params.thinking`, the global
default, and provider/model defaults. Returning the merged global value through
those override-sensitive paths would make the global default incorrectly win
over a per-model setting.

This change separates the two contracts:

- `resolveAgentConfig()` now returns the documented merged value.
- `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` returns only the explicit per-agent
  value for precedence-sensitive runtime paths.

The command, reply model-selection, subagent inheritance, gateway session, and
startup-summary paths use the explicit helper where provenance matters.

## User Impact

Consumers of `resolveAgentConfig()` can now rely on a listed agent inheriting
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`. Existing runtime precedence remains intact:

1. session or message override
2. explicit per-agent default
3. per-model `params.thinking`
4. global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`
5. provider/model default

Explicit `off` values remain authoritative because the merge uses nullish, not
truthy, fallback semantics.

## Breaking Changes

None expected. This restores the documented merged-config contract while
preserving the existing runtime precedence order.

## Implementation

- Add `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` at the agent-scope owner boundary.
- Merge `thinkingDefault` in `resolveAgentConfig()` with agent-over-global
  nullish precedence.
- Route precedence-sensitive callers through the explicit override helper.
- Add focused tests for merged inheritance, explicit `off`, and a listed agent
  whose per-model thinking setting must still outrank the global default.

## Code-Path Analysis

- Owner: `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts`
- Public facade: `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Runtime callers: `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`,
  `src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`, `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`,
  `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- Adjacent precedence owner: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`
- Tests: `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`,
  `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`, plus existing command,
  subagent, gateway-session, and startup-summary coverage
- Contract: `src/config/types.agents.ts` and `docs/tools/thinking.md`

## Mainline Comparison

- Official base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@ff9b29167352b5896c772dfcff9176fb003f530d`
- Base fetched/verified: July 17, 2026, 04:00 UTC
- Current main still returned only `entry.thinkingDefault` from the merged
  resolver. Recent same-surface changes did not implement this provenance split.

## Branch/Base Provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@ff9b29167352b5896c772dfcff9176fb003f530d`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/109276-thinking-default-fallback@06295d97214c83a8e72fbcd763792b4011d301d8`
- The head branch was created/replayed directly from the official base.
- The fork default branch was not used as the implementation baseline and was
  not modified by this work.

## Dependency/Contract Verification

No external dependency contract changed. The configuration type already states
that `agents.list[].thinkingDefault` overrides
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`, and the thinking documentation already
defines per-model thinking ahead of the global default. The implementation now
preserves both contracts explicitly.

## Labels Considered

- `agents`
- `P2`
- `impact:auth-provider`
- `merge-risk: compatibility` because configuration-default precedence is
  compatibility-sensitive

These are suggestions only; this contribution does not claim maintainer label
authority.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.test.ts`

## Evidence Source Map

- Exact-head downstream CI: [Evidence workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29553799447)
  - Head: `06295d97214c83a8e72fbcd763792b4011d301d8`
  - Base: `ff9b29167352b5896c772dfcff9176fb003f530d`

  - Covers focused unit tests, changed-file checks, formatting, type checks, and

## Sanitized Logs

```text
Explicit override: listed agent thinkingDefault=off -> off
Precedence guard: listed agent without override + per-model thinking + global default -> per-model value

```

No credentials, hostnames, internal paths, account identifiers, or private
runtime data are included.

- Security/privacy: no authorization, secret, persistence, or transport changes.

target.title: fix(config-cli,secrets): typed ExitError, JSON error output, and consistent stateDir for audit .env
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

### config get --json

`openclaw config get <path> --json` produces empty stdout when the config path does not exist. It only writes a text error message to stderr and exits with code 1. Automated consumers (scripts, CI) that pipe stdout expecting JSON receive nothing, making error handling unreliable.

### Secrets audit & apply .env path

The secrets audit and apply operations resolve the state directory for auth/model stores but re-resolve it for `.env`. If directory availability changes between calls (canonical `.openclaw` vs legacy `.clawdbot` directory appearing or disappearing), one operation can inspect or mutate two different state roots for the same run.

In `apply.ts` specifically, `projectPlanState` resolves `stateDir` once and uses it for config targets, auth stores, and legacy auth stores — but `scrubEnvFiles` calls `resolveStateDir` independently, so a root switch mid-operation can scrub a different `.env` and leave the intended plaintext credential untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

### config get --json

The `--json` flag implies machine-readable output on stdout. When a path is not found, the command now emits a structured JSON error on stdout, consistent with how `runConfigValidate` and `handleConfigMutationError` handle JSON-mode errors. The exit signal detection was also migrated from a fragile `__exit__:` string prefix match to the repository's typed `ExitError` contract.

### Secrets audit .env path

Reuse the already-resolved `stateDir` variable for constructing the `.env` path in `audit.ts`.

### Secrets apply .env path

Pass the `stateDir` already resolved by `projectPlanState` (line 296) into `scrubEnvFiles` instead of letting `scrubEnvFiles` call `resolveStateDir` again. This ensures auth stores (auth-profiles.json, auth.json) and `.env` are handled under the same state root for the entire apply operation.

## User Impact

- `openclaw config get nonexistent.path --json` now outputs `{"error": "Config path not found: nonexistent.path"}` to stdout (exit code 1)
- Non-JSON mode behavior is unchanged: error goes to stderr as before
- Secrets audit consistently reads `.env` from the same state directory as auth and model stores
- Secrets apply scrubs `.env` under the same state root as auth stores — no root-switch gap

## Evidence

### Real CLI proof — config get --json

**stdout:**
```
{
  "error": "Config path not found: nonexistent.path"
}
```
**stderr:** (build bootstrap logs only, no config command error output)
```
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs config get nonexistent.path --json
[openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: dirty_watched_tree - dirty watched source tree).
...
```
**Exit code:** 1

### Real CLI proof — secrets audit

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR pnpm openclaw secrets audit --json
{
  "version": 1,
  "status": "findings",
  "filesScanned": [
    "/tmp/.../openclaw/.env",
    "/tmp/.../openclaw/openclaw.json"
  ],
  "summary": { "plaintextCount": 2, ... },
  "findings": [
    { "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND", "file": ".../openclaw.json", ... },
    { "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND", "file": ".../openclaw/.env", "jsonPath": "$env.OPENAI_API_KEY", ... }
  ]
}
```
Exit code: 0

### Real CLI proof — secrets apply (root-switch)

**Setup:** HOME contains both `.openclaw` (canonical) and `.clawdbot` (legacy) directories. Both have `.env` files with plaintext keys, plus `openclaw.json` with a plaintext `apiKey`.

**Before apply:**
```
-- .openclaw/.env (canonical, SHOULD be scrubbed) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-prod-plaintext-should-be-scrubbed
UNRELATED=keep-me

-- .clawdbot/.env (legacy, must NOT be touched) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-legacy-should-NOT-be-touched
UNRELATED=legacy-value

-- openclaw.json --
"apiKey": "sk-prod-plaintext-should-be-scrubbed"
```

**Command:**
```
$ HOME=$TMPHOME pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from plan.json
Secrets applied. Updated 2 file(s).
```

**After apply:**
```
-- .openclaw/.env (verify scrubbed) --
UNRELATED=keep-me

-- .clawdbot/.env (verify UNTOUCHED) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-legacy-should-NOT-be-touched
UNRELATED=legacy-value

-- openclaw.json --
"apiKey": {
  "source": "env",
  "provider": "default",
  "id": "OPENAI_API_KEY"
}
```

**Verification:**
- ✅ `.openclaw/.env` was scrubbed (plaintext key removed)
- ✅ `.openclaw/.env` preserved `UNRELATED=keep-me`
- ✅ `.clawdbot/.env` was NOT touched (legacy key still present)
- ✅ `.clawdbot/.env` preserved `UNRELATED=legacy-value`
- ✅ `openclaw.json` plaintext `apiKey` replaced with `SecretRef`

The plan targets `models.providers.openai.apiKey` with `scrubEnv: true`. `resolveStateDir` returns `.openclaw` when both directories exist, and the apply operation uses that single resolved `stateDir` for both auth stores and `.env` scrubbing. The legacy `.clawdbot/.env` is never touched.

### Tests

- `pnpm test src/secrets/apply.test.ts` — **31/31 passed** (includes new root-switch regression: "uses the same resolved stateDir for .env scrubbing as for auth stores")
- `pnpm test src/secrets/audit.test.ts` — **26/26 passed**
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — **130/130 passed**
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts` — **5/5 passed**

### Lint & Format

- oxlint: clean (`src/secrets/apply.ts`, `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`)
- oxfmt: clean

### New regression test — apply root-switch

The test sets up a HOME where both `.openclaw` and `.clawdbot` exist. `resolveStateDir` returns `.openclaw` when both exist (it checks `.openclaw` first). The test:

1. Writes a `.env` with a plaintext secret in `.openclaw` (canonical)
2. Writes a different `.env` with a dummy secret in `.clawdbot` (legacy)
3. Runs `secrets apply` with `scrubEnv: true`
4. Asserts `.openclaw/.env` was scrubbed (secret removed)
5. Asserts `.clawdbot/.env` was NOT touched (secret still present)

This proves one apply operation cannot switch roots mid-operation.

### Review findings addressed (revise round)

- **[P2] Reuse the operation's resolved state directory in apply** — `src/secrets/apply.ts:734`: `scrubEnvFiles` now accepts `stateDir` parameter and uses it instead of calling `resolveStateDir` again. Call site at line 341 passes the `stateDir` resolved on line 296.
- **[P1] Add root-switch regression** — `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`: New test "uses the same resolved stateDir for .env scrubbing as for auth stores" proves the invariant.

### Behavior addressed

- CLI JSON errors now reliably reach stdout consumers
- Exit signal contract migrated from `__exit__:` string sentinel to typed `ExitError`
- Audit `.env` lookup uses resolved `stateDir` instead of re-resolving
- Apply `.env` scrubbing uses the same `stateDir` as auth stores — single-root invariant

### What was not tested

- macOS-specific `realpath` symlink behavior (Linux CI parity)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing a Pi session catalog could receive malformed Unicode in long tool-call arguments when the 20,000-character display limit landed inside an emoji's UTF-16 surrogate pair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog now uses the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper before appending its ellipsis. After the fix:

## What Problem This Solves

Every realtime voice consumer re-plumbed the same session wiring around the shared bridge/talk primitives: talk-session controller creation and event ring capture, output-activity tracking with echo-suppression window bookkeeping, transcript recording with assistant-echo filtering, agent talkback queue construction, forced-consult coordination, and barge-in-to-output-flush coupling. Google Meet carried this twice (agent/STT and bidi engines), voice-call once, Discord once — four hand-maintained copies of the same invariants.

## Why This Change Was Made

Phase 3 of the voice-stack consolidation (follows #109413, #109466). New `src/talk/realtime-session-harness.ts` (`createRealtimeVoiceSessionHarness`, exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice`) owns the transport-agnostic session shape: talk lifecycle helpers with injected payload builders, input/output audio recording with echo-suppression windows and suppressed-byte accounting, bounded transcript + bridge-event capture, talkback queue, forced-consult coordinator, health snapshot assembly, and `handleBargeIn` with flush-generation fallback (generalizing Meet's clear-count pattern).

Adopted by Google Meet (both engines) and voice-call's realtime handler; their local wiring is deleted. Consumers keep audio I/O, format conversion, provider resolution, prompts, and pacing.

Discord adoption is deliberately a follow-up: the mapping was verified against `extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime.ts` (bridge creation, talkback, forced-consult state, output tracker, barge-in paths all map onto the harness; speaker attribution, wake-name policy, Opus conversion, preroll, and player lifecycle stay Discord-side) and no harness API gap was found.

## User Impact

None intended. Talk-event shapes and payloads, health fields, echo-suppression timings, log lines, and barge-in behavior are unchanged per consumer.

## Evidence

- New harness unit tests (talk-event ordering, echo-suppression window, talkback delegation, barge-in flush fallback); the voice-call forced-consult cancellation regression test was adapted to drive the harness-owned coordinator (review-found, restored — late native consult is terminally answered as cancelled without invoking the consult handler).

target.title: fix(video-generation): DashScope downloads hang when CDN body stalls after headers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two issues with DashScope-compatible video downloads:

1. **Stalled CDN body hang**: After headers returned, no chunk-idle timeout was wired into `readResponseWithLimit`, so a stalled body could wait the full request budget instead of failing with a clear idle timeout.
2. **Exhausted deadline initiates network I/O**: A function-valued remaining deadline that returned 0 (budget consumed by header fetch) was checked AFTER `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` had already sent bytes over the wire. The guard now runs before fetch.

Affected workflow: `runDashscopeVideoGenerationTask` → `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` → `readResponseWithLimit`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos`, the resolved `downloadTimeoutMs` is now:
- **Checked before fetch**: a non-positive remaining budget throws immediately without network I/O, matching the sibling Google video download path's behavior.
- **Passed as `chunkTimeoutMs`** + `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`, so stalled bodies fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` deadline.

`fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` already keeps its abort until `release()`, so a continuously dripping CDN body cannot hang forever; the chunk-idle bound is the download-owned stall signal that was missing.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded`, `readResponseWithLimit`, or `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.

Collision check: no open PR on `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` / `src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts`.

## User Impact

- Stalled DashScope video downloads fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic request timeout or full-budget wait.
- Already-exhausted remaining budgets fail immediately without network I/O.
- Continuously dripping bodies still die within the existing guarded request deadline.

## Evidence

Exact head: `920b47be7e9a11c1fbb78845226d51aca97afdf8`

`oxfmt --check src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ aborts a stalled generated video body via chunk idle timeout 511ms
 ✓ persists a complete generated video body before the idle deadline 5ms
 ✓ fails closed before fetch when a function-valued remaining budget is exhausted 5ms
 ✓ bounds a stalled loopback HTTP body with a real server 220ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Key contract changes

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Exhausted deadline checked after `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` (network I/O already initiated) | Checked before fetch — throws immediately, `fetchFn` not called |
| Body had no chunk-idle timeout → stalled bodies hit generic request timeout | `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` wired → `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` |

### Loopback proof

Real `http.createServer` returns HTTP 200 + one chunk then stalls. Real `fetch` + real `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` with `timeoutMs: 200` rejects within 5s (~220ms observed) — bounded, not an indefinite hang.

### Not tested

Live DashScope CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

## What changed

- add a collapsed 15-minute throughput disclosure to both review admission and result publication
- keep both disclosures visually aligned with four lane-specific metrics and the same retry-amplification footer

- Review Arrival includes admitted work and shed demand, matching the Net review rate incoming definition.

## Summary

- allow empty or comment-only `.npmrc` and `bunfig.toml` files during target dependency setup

## Root cause

After the sparse-checkout repair in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/630, automerge workers reached target toolchain setup but failed because the validation policy rejected the mere presence of `.npmrc`. OpenClaw retains a comment-only `.npmrc` so Docker COPY paths stay stable, as seen in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29543195892.

This change permits only text that cannot affect dependency installation. Any real configuration remains rejected, preserving the target-controlled network boundary.

## Impact

OpenClaw automerge jobs can prepare the target toolchain without rejecting the repository's inert `.npmrc`. No service restart is required after merge; affected PRs can be retriggered with `@clawsweeper automerge`.
